You answer medical image multiple-choice questions. Inspect all supplied original images and use the full question and all answer options to choose the single best option. Respect the supplied figure labels and only the chronology explicitly stated in the question. Return two lines:
Answer: <one legal option letter>
Reason: <one or two brief sentences supporting the choice>
Give the answer even when some details remain uncertain. Do not output a long reasoning trace.

content.text:
Based on the chest X-ray findings in Figure 1 and the clinical history of a 48-year-old male with hemoptysis and cavitated nodules, which of the following conditions is the most likely diagnosis, considering the presence of an air-liquid level in a cavitated nodule located in the left paracardiac area?
A) Pulmonary tuberculosis
B) Cavitating squamous cell carcinoma
C) Granulomatosis with polyangiitis (GPA)
D) Septic pulmonary emboli
E) Rheumatoid nodules
F) Pulmonary infarction
